land.text: the Kalaa, where Emir Abderrahmane withdrew after the Spanish took Béjaïa in 1510

predecessors.note: Abderrahmane settled the Kalaa in the second half of the 15th century (no year); the page says the kingdom 'owed its founding' to his withdrawal.

land.text: the Kalaa and the Medjana: 'The Kalaa itself, impregnable since the 16th century, surrendered on 22 July 1871'

successors.note: The page adds that Boumezrag was arrested at Ouargla on 20 January 1872 and that the expropriation of the Mokranis 'marked the final extinction of their political role'.

capitals.name: Kalaa of Ait Abbas
capitals.note: The page names the capital as the Kalaa, 'a citadel in the Bibans mountains', and gives no coordinates. The dot is the researcher's estimate inside the Bibans, in the north of the Bordj Bou Arreridj province (bbox 4.3-5.17 E, 35.85-36.29 N).

correction.text: the Kalaa in the Bibans and the Medjana country, taken as the Bordj Bou Arréridj province

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page has no area; it says the kingdom's influence went 'from the valley of the Soummam to the Sahara' and a principality 'from the Sahel River to Hodna' (neither dated). The province is the researcher's reading of Bibans and Medjana.

correction.text: the Medjana and the Hodna, with the Saharan oases Biskra, Touggourt and Laghouat reached under Ahmed Amokrane

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Under Ahmed Amokrane (1559-1596 infobox) the kingdom 'reached its territorial peak' and extended influence south to the oases of Tolga, Biskra, Touggourt and Laghouat (no year). The page says the Hodna tribes were removed from the Mokrani's control in 1849, so Hodna is kept to 1848. The oasis circles are influence, not frontier, and are kept at 40 km; Tolga is not in the gazetteer.

correction.text: the Medjana, after the Hodna tribes were removed from the Mokrani's control in 1849

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'In 1849 Hodna tribes were removed from his control' (Ahmed Mokrani, khalifa of the Medjana under the French since 30 September 1838); the oasis circles are dropped for lack of any later page.

region.text: the Kalaa and the Medjana, Bordj Bou Arréridj province

ledger.note: 1510: the Kalaa kingdom begins. The infobox gives 1510; the page says it 'owed its founding' to the withdrawal of the Hafsid emir Aberrahmane after the Spanish took Béjaïa in 1510. Abderrahmane had settled the Kalaa in the second half of the 15th century (no year).

region.text: the Hodna and the Saharan oases Biskra, Touggourt and Laghouat

ledger.note: 1559-1596 (bridge): Ahmed Amokrane extends the kingdom to the Sahara. The page gives no year: the kingdom 'reached its territorial peak' in his reign (1559-1596 infobox) and his influence reached 'the oases of Tolga, Biskra, Touggourt, and Laghouat'. 1559 is his accession, after Hassan Pasha killed his brother Abdelaziz in battle.
1849: the French detach the Hodna tribes. 'In 1849, Hodna tribes were removed from his control'; on 15 April 1845 a royal ordinance had already 'detached' tribes from the khalifa's command.

22 July 1871: the Kalaa surrenders. 'The Kalaa itself, impregnable since the 16th century, surrendered on 22 July 1871' after the Mokrani revolt (joined 15 March 1871; Mohamed Mokrani died 5 May 1871); the infobox ends the revolt in 1872.

wars.name: Algiers against the Kalaa
wars.outcome: The Barbarossa brothers attacked Abdelaziz near Béjaïa in 1516 and he submitted; the Regency made the Kalaa's lord its khalifa in the Medjana in 1542; he repulsed two Turkish expeditions in 1550; the Kalaa was attacked in 1552-1553; Hassan Pasha attacked it in 1559 and Abdelaziz died on the second day of the battle.
wars.note: The page's Spanish alliance of Abdelaziz is undated; Béjaïa passed to Salah Rais in 1555.

wars.name: Khizr Pasha's siege and Ahmed Amokrane's campaign against Algiers
wars.outcome: Khizr Pasha besieged the Kalaa for two months in 1590 and failed; Ahmed Amokrane paid 30,000 douros for recognition of independence; he besieged Algiers for eleven days in 1598 and was killed in 1600 after beating Soliman Veneziano.
wars.note: The Ahmed Ait Mokran page gives 1598 for the occupation of Algiers, c. 1600 for his death at Fort Hamza near Bouira, and has the infobox death in 1596.

wars.name: Battle of Guidjel
wars.outcome: On 20 September 1638 the tribes and Constantine fought the Pasha of Algiers; the victory led to independence from Algiers.

wars.name: Mokrani revolt
wars.outcome: The revolt began on 15 March 1871 (the Rahmaniyya joined on 8 April); Mohamed Mokrani died on 5 May 1871 and the Kalaa surrendered on 22 July.

certainty.note: The pages give no frontier; the Bordj Bou Arréridj and M'Sila provinces and the 40 km oasis circles are the researcher's. The Kalaa's status towards Algiers (khalifa, tributary, independent) and towards the French (khalifa of the Medjana from 1838) changed several times and is not drawn.

notes: Cliopatria has no Kalaa row. The page's infobox lists rulers Abdelaziz Ou Abbas 1510-1559 and Boumezrag 1871-1872 and says the principality reached 'from the valley of the Soummam to the Sahara'; no area is given. Status towards Algiers, from the page: submission to the Barbarossas in 1516, khalifa of the Medjana from 1542, 'independence' recognised by Khizr Pasha in 1590 for 30,000 douros and again after the Guidjel victory in 1638, tribute and the ouadia under Bouzid (1680-1735), vassals of the Bey of Constantine in the late 18th century (no year); after the French took Constantine in 1837 Ahmed Mokrani became khalifa of the Medjana on 30 September 1838. These are suzerainty events for the Regency, Constantine and French dossiers, and none is drawn here; the Regency dossier starts in 1706, so the early wars use its slug without a dossier for the years. The Mokrani dynasty's end is 1871 here (surrender of the Kalaa) against 1872 in the infobox. The Kuku kingdom (kingdom-of-kuku) fought on Algiers' side in 1559. Béjaïa, held by Spain 1510 (1509 on the Hafsid dossier) to 1555, is not in the kingdom's circle.
